question: Which contract should shared-gateway multi-agent memory-wiki isolation use: generic `agents.list[].plugins` overrides, a memory-wiki-owned per-agent vault resolver, or explicitly unsupported shared-gateway wiki isolation?
rationale: The evidence proves the current single-vault behavior, but the permanent fix must choose config precedence, no-context CLI/gateway behavior, SecretRef/config handling, and security semantics before implementation.

options.title: Plugin-owned vault isolation first
options.body: Add a memory-wiki-owned per-agent vault contract now, with explicit no-agent behavior and compatibility with a future generic plugin override API.

options.title: Generic per-agent plugin config
options.body: Implement `agents.list[].plugins` as the canonical config override layer and adapt memory-wiki to consume it, accepting broader plugin SDK compatibility work.

options.title: Keep shared vault unsupported
options.body: Document that memory-wiki is process-global in shared gateway mode and route isolation needs to separate gateway/profile deployments.

recommendation.title: Plugin-owned vault isolation first
recommendation.body: Add a memory-wiki-owned per-agent vault contract now, with explicit no-agent behavior and compatibility with a future generic plugin override API.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans plugin config, runtime, security, and upgrade policy surfaces where recent history points to steipete as the best available owner.
